name: Sega Mega Drive / Genesis
description: Sega's 16-bit console, released in Japan in 1988 and sold as the Genesis in North America. Sonic the Hedgehog and its fast arcade-style games took on Nintendo directly, and the console was especially popular in North America, Europe and Brazil.

specs.memory: 64 KB RAM / 64 KB VRAM / 8 KB Z80 RAM

curiosities: The Z80 also lets it play Master System games through the Power Base Converter.
Tectoy has kept making versions of it in Brazil for decades.
The Genesis name was used in North America because Sega could not secure the Mega Drive trademark there.
The 32X and Mega-CD add-ons could be connected at the same time.
story: Sega built the Mega Drive on its System 16 arcade boards: a Motorola 68000 with a Z80 for sound. It launched in Japan in October 1988, where it stayed behind the PC Engine and the Famicom.

In North America it became the Genesis in 1989, with 'Genesis does what Nintendon't' advertising and arcade ports. Under Tom Kalinske, Sega bundled Sonic the Hedgehog from 1991 and for a while outsold the Super NES there, with sports games from EA and a cooler, older image.
It sold around 30 million units, stayed popular in Brazil for decades, and its music, from the Yamaha FM chip, is loved to this day.
